flagged.evidence: The definition supplies a “nonzero simple-pole residue Z_a” and then uses Z_a^{1/2} in the pole factorization and Z_a^{-1/2} in the normalized residue, but does not supply a square root or a branch convention. Since the data allow complex residues, Z_a alone does not select a root; changing the root changes the amplitude’s sign for that channel.

The definition calls the entries U_Aa “field-to-channel overlap coefficients” and requires only that U be invertible. It gives no equation relating U to the fields, channels, Green functions, or pole residues; the stated factorization uses only Z_a and does not use U. Thus the entries are merely an arbitrary invertible matrix, which does not define the named overlap or how component fields correspond to channel poles.

An admissible field-coordinate change is defined only as a “local, parity-preserving formal map” with an inverse modulo the truncation. The definition then says that for the standard product measure its factor is the Berezinian of DF. No differentiability or other regularity ensuring DF exists is imposed, so the Berezinian claim is not licensed for every map admitted by the definition.
